subject: Schedule: Performance & Latency Benchmarking Deep-Dive — Nova Analytics
messages:
From: Alex Turner <alex.turner@novaanalytics.com>
To: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Sarah Lee <sarah.lee@novaanalytics.com>
Date: 2026-03-05T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Performance/latency benchmarking deep-dive — proposed session

Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the product demo last week — the team asked for a follow-up focused on performance and latency. We'd like a 60–90 minute technical deep-dive to:

- Walk through Redwood's serving architecture for low-latency paths (KV cache, batching strategies).
- Review proposed load-test plans (target tokens/sec, concurrency profiles, seq lengths).
- Align on success criteria and observability (tracing, per-token latency SLOs).

Our initial availability windows this week: Thu 3/5 4:00–6:00 PM PT or Fri 3/6 between 9:00–11:30 AM PT.

Attached a short list of our perf requirements and the top 3 workloads we want validated. Please let me know who from your team should join (engineer + solutions engineer ideally), and whether you prefer a recorded meeting + test run or a live run with us watching.

Regards,
Alex Turner
Senior Platform Engineer, Nova Analytics
[Attachment: perf_requirements.pdf (application/pdf)]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-05T17:09:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Performance/latency benchmarking deep-dive — proposed session

Hi Alex — great to hear this is a priority. We're happy to run a focused benchmarking review.

Quick answers up front:
- We can do a 75-minute session (45 min deep-dive + 30 min live test planning).
- Ideal attendees from our side: me (solutions lead), Vivek (serving/runtime), and Stephanie (SRE/observability).
- We recommend: a short recorded walk-through of architecture + one live canary load test in your environment, then a follow-up dedicated load sweep if you want full throughput numbers.

Would Thu 3/5 4:30 PM PT work for a 75-min slot? If not, Fri 3/6 10:00 AM PT is also free for us.

Also attached: a draft test plan template (redwood-perf-test-plan-v1.docx) with sections to fill for seq length distribution, tokenization details, and metric dashboard links. Could you populate the top-of-form fields ahead of the call (seq len, expected peak concurrency, preferred target metrics)? That will let Vivek size the canary run appropriately.

Thanks — I'll send a calendar invite after you confirm.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood-perf-test-plan-v1.docx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document)]

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Alex Turner <alex.turner@novaanalytics.com>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-06T09:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Performance/latency benchmarking deep-dive — proposed session

Alex / Marissa — quick technical note before we lock the calendar:

- For the canary run, we usually target 1) short-seq (<=64 tokens) throughput and 2) mid-seq (256 tokens) tail latency. Suggested initial targets: 8k tokens/sec aggregate for short-seq and 1.5k tokens/sec for mid-seq across a 4 GPU pool (these scale linearly).
- Please confirm whether you want KV cache warmup included in the live run (adds ~15–30s warmup per model). If you have a mix of prompt prefixes that can share prefixes we can show cache hit effects.
- We'll use our load harness (kv-cache-loadscript.yml) and stream sampling to feed metrics into your Grafana dashboard; if you can add a temporary read-only dashboard link we can push traces.

If those numbers look off for your expected production profile, share a target and we'll adjust.

— Vivek
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime
[Attachment: kv-cache-loadscript.yml (text/yaml)]

Thanks — heads up, I need to push the meeting by a bit: I have a conflicting customer outage call on Thu afternoon. Can we move to Fri 3/6 at 10:00 AM PT? Attendees on our side will be myself, Sarah (platform), and Tom from infra (TBD).

Also, two quick questions:
1) During the live canary, do you recommend running canary traffic against our dedicated capacity or a temporary hosted slot? We prefer dedicated but want to avoid impacting production.
2) Can you outline the expected deliverables post-session (raw token throughput numbers, per-model latency p95/p99, and a recommended quantization profile if relevant)?

On the attachments — I'll fill the redwood test plan fields and send back before EOD today.

Alex
